finding.claim: Remote HTML returned by the embed adapter is emitted verbatim, bypassing the html_input filter. If an allowed domain serves attacker-controlled content, that becomes script injection in the rendered page. Conditional on allowed_domains including a domain that hosts attacker content, such as a wildcard-subdomain platform.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled page on an allowed host, reached via an https:// embed line in the Markdown input (src/Extension/Embed/EmbedStartParser.php:34)

trace.note: Attacker-supplied https:// URL line becomes an Embed block
Remote extractor->code->html stored as embed code
Stored embed code emitted with no escaping and no html_input check

finding.guards_checked: DomainFilteringAdapter.php:40-61 restricts hosts only if allowed_domains is set (EmbedExtension.php:39-41), and suffix matching lets any subdomain of an allowed domain through. No sanitisation of embed HTML anywhere on the path. html_input (HtmlInlineRenderer.php:44, HtmlBlockRenderer.php:44) does not apply to embeds.

finding.claim: The allowlist is checked only on the URL as written. The underlying fetch library may follow HTTP redirects, so an allowed host can redirect the server to an internal or metadata address, bypassing the filter. Plausible, not verified: embed/embed is not vendored in this repository.
finding.source: Attacker-chosen https:// embed URL on an allowed host, or any URL when allowed_domains is empty
finding.sink: Server-side HTTP request made by the embed library at src/Extension/Embed/Bridge/OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:43 (getMulti)

trace.note: isAllowed() checks only the initial host; no re-check after redirect
Host suffix match against allowed domains
Library fetches the URL, following redirects unless configured otherwise

finding.guards_checked: DomainFilteringAdapter.php:44-49 enforces http/https scheme. Host comparison is lowercased and dot-anchored (line 55). Nothing validates resolved IPs or redirect targets. With allowed_domains empty (EmbedExtension.php:39), there is no host filter at all.
